role: Chairman, Department of Biology, Furman University; author of flora pamphlet
stance_basis: conducted botanical survey for applicant and directed transplanting of rare plants, implying acceptance of project with mitigation measures
summary: Dr. C. Leland Rodgers, Chairman of the Department of Biology at Furman University, conducted a botanical survey of the Bad Creek project area in 1973, identifying rare plant species and recommending relocation of some specimens. He directed the transplanting of ginseng, American climbing fern, wintergreen, witch alder, and lysimachia to areas outside the project, with observations in May 1975 showing the transplants thriving. His involvement suggests support for the project contingent on appropriate mitigation of impacts to rare flora.
complaint_summary: Dr. Rodgers and J.E. Green Jr. of Furman University conducted a 1973 botanical survey of the project area, identifying three major plant communities and four rare or uncommon plant species, and recommending relocation of some specimens of ginseng, American climbing fern, and wintergreen to similar nearby habitats.
summary_quote: Dr. C. Leland Rodgers (Exhibit W, Appendix 6) has stated that Duke's plans for constructing transmission lines should result in these Oconee bells not being disturbed.

mentions.quote: The Applicant arranged for a botanical survey of the project area by Dr. C. Leland Rodgers and J.E. Green, Jr., of Furman University.
Dr. C. Leland Rodgers (Exhibit W, Appendix 6) has stated that Duke's plans for constructing transmission lines should result in these Oconee bells not being disturbed.
mentions.role_as_written: botanist/authority on flora of project area

mentions.quote: Concerning the transmission lines, Dr. Rodgers stated that "the only plant along the route that deserves special consideration is Shortia galacifola." However, as noted by Dr. Rodgers, Duke's present plans for transmission line construction should leave the Shortia undisturbed.
By DR. C. LELAND RODGERS Chairman, Department of Biology Furman University
